darshanas.name: Nyāya darśana
darshanas.blurb: The school of logic and epistemology: the sūtras of Gautama, their classical commentaries, the ‘new’ Nyāya of Gaṅgeśa, and the Nyāya-Vaiśeṣika primer that students still begin with.

nyaya.title: Nyāyasūtra with Vātsyāyana’s Nyāyabhāṣya
nyaya.author: Gautama (Akṣapāda), with the commentary of Vātsyāyana (Pakṣilasvāmin)
nyaya.blurb: The root text of the school, 528 sūtras in five adhyāyas, with the oldest surviving commentary.

nyaya-tatparya.title: Nyāyasūtra with Vācaspati Miśra’s Tātparyaṭīkā
nyaya-tatparya.author: Vācaspati Miśra (10th century), on Uddyotakara’s Nyāyavārttika
nyaya-tatparya.blurb: Vācaspati’s ‘commentary on the purport’ of the Vārttika, the great defence of Nyāya against the Buddhist logicians, set out under each sūtra of Gautama.

tattvacintamani.title: Tattvacintāmaṇi of Gaṅgeśa · Śabdakhaṇḍa
tattvacintamani.author: Gaṅgeśa Upādhyāya (14th century)
tattvacintamani.blurb: The founding work of Navya-Nyāya. This book on verbal testimony runs from the defence of śabda as a means of knowledge to the debate over what words denote.

tarkasangraha.title: Tarkasaṃgraha of Annaṃbhaṭṭa
tarkasangraha.author: Annaṃbhaṭṭa (17th century)
tarkasangraha.blurb: The classic primer of Nyāya-Vaiśeṣika: the seven categories and the four means of knowledge in 81 short sections.

tarkasangraha-dipika.title: Tarkasaṃgraha with the Dīpikā, Prakāśikā and Bālapriyā
tarkasangraha-dipika.author: Annaṃbhaṭṭa’s own Dīpikā, Nīlakaṇṭha Bhaṭṭa’s Prakāśikā, and N. S. Rāmānuja Tātācārya’s Bālapriyā
tarkasangraha-dipika.blurb: The Tarkasaṃgraha with its author’s own commentary and two layers of sub-commentary, followed by Kṛṣṇa Tātācārya’s Prasāraṇā on the Prakāśikā.
